issues.failure_explanation: Exactness is assumed only on the family {lambda f* : lambda in (lambda_-,lambda_+)} (resp. {f*(alpha . + beta)}), so the h-expansion for f = lambda f* yields q(f-bar)=f(a) and q^{(0,1)}(f-bar)=1/2 only at the diagonal points lambda(f*(a),f*(a)) covered by that family (Lemma lem:aff states exactly this: the equalities hold 'for all values of f-bar with f(a) in the range of f*'). The proof of Lemma lem:noworse nevertheless concludes these identities 'for all f-bar' and then claims o(h^2) for every f in C^2(a,a+h); Corollary cor:pders states the identities at an arbitrary f-bar; Theorem thm:construct quantifies its error bound over all f in C^4(R) although f*^{-1}, hence q_1, is defined only on R = f*(R). At uncovered arguments q is unconstrained: modifying q off the covered set (e.g. by a bump in f(a) that vanishes there) preserves scalable/affine exactness on f* while making the error for f with f(a) at the modified point equal to Theta(h), not o(h^2).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the local condition that the node values of f lie in the set covered by the exact family (f(a) in (lambda_-,lambda_+)f*(a) for scalably exact rules, f(a) in range(f*) for affinely exact rules, and f mapping into R for thm:construct), or strengthen the hypotheses to exactness for all scalings and shifts with f* onto R, so that the identities hold on the whole diagonal.
issues.overall_effect: The o(h^2) conclusions of lem:noworse and lem:aff, the diagonal identities of cor:pders and the o(h^4) error claim of thm:construct as quantified over all f are unsupported outside the arguments covered by the target family (for thm:construct the rule is not even defined there); cor:added-1 is affected in the same way in addition to its own defect.
issues.title: Identities obtained on one exact family are asserted at all arguments
issues.why_classification: The repair is a standard local condition (or a one-line strengthening of the exactness hypothesis); the conclusions, their rates and the intended use for f near the target family all survive, and no new lemma, construction or argument is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Substituting this into the Taylor expansion of $q(f(a),f(b))$ around
to reduce the integration error of the trapezoidal rule by using the known

issues.failure_explanation: The proof computes q^{(0,2)} only at the single point f-bar* = (f*(a),f*(a)) (in fact the h^3 matching for lambda f* gives q^{(0,2)}(lambda f-bar*) = -f*''(a)/(6 lambda f*'(a)^2), which varies along the diagonal) and then inserts this value into the expansion of q(f(a),f(b)) around f(b) = f(a), which requires q^{(0,2)} at the generally different point (f(a),f(a)). The stated constant coefficient -(1/12)f*''(a)/f*'(a)^2 is therefore wrong whenever f(a) != f*(a). Concretely, for the paper's own rule eq:qexp (f*(x)=e^x, a=0) and f(x)=2e^x, which lies in the exact family, q(2,2e^h) = 2(e^h-1)/h = 2 + h + h^2/3 + O(h^3), whereas the claimed right-hand side is (2+2e^h)/2 - (1/12)(2e^h-2)^2 + o(h^2) = 2 + h + h^2/6 + o(h^2).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the constant coefficient by its value at the expansion point: the quadratic term is -(1/12)[f*''(u)/f*'(u)^2](f(b)-f(a))^2 with u = f*^{-1}(f(a)) (equivalently -(1/12) f*''(a)f*(a)/(f*'(a)^2 f(a)) along the scaling ray at fixed a), and use this corrected coefficient in the proposed improved trapezoidal rule.
issues.overall_effect: Corollary cor:added-1 is false as stated, and the 'improved trapezoidal rule' proposed immediately after it repeats the wrong second-order correction, so it does not deliver the promised error reduction for functions close to lambda f* with lambda != 1.
issues.title: Second-order term of q uses the curvature of f* at the wrong point
issues.why_classification: The formula that is the content of the corollary must be replaced by a point-dependent one and the advertised improved rule re-derived with it; the repair is contained and preserves the second-order expansion, its rate and the intended application, but it changes the mathematical claim rather than merely adding a hypothesis.

issues.failure_explanation: Writing q_1(x,x+u) = x + u/2 + (1/2)A(x)u^2 + (1/6)B(x)u^3 + ... with A = q_1^{(0,2)}, B = q_1^{(0,3)} on the diagonal, the combination alpha_1 h q_1(f(a),f(a+h)) + alpha_2[h q_1(f(a),f(a+h/2)) + h q_1(f(a+h/2),f(a+h))] has f'(a)^3 B h^4 coefficient (4 alpha_1+alpha_2)/24, not 4(2 alpha_1+alpha_2)/48 as displayed (for alpha_1=0, alpha_2=2/3 the two half-intervals contribute h^4 B f'(a)^3/24 in total, while the displayed formula gives /12), and the expansion omits the term alpha_2 h^4 f'(a)^3 A'(f(a))/16 arising because the second half-interval is expanded at f(a+h/2). With alpha_1=-1/3, alpha_2=2/3 the true h^4 error coefficient is f'(a)^3[A'/24 - B/36], which vanishes only through the unstated identity B = (3/2)A' that follows from eq:construct (e.g. f*=e^x: A=-1/(6x), B=1/(4x^2)). Thus the printed expansion is wrong and the o(h^4) conclusion does not follow from it (it happens to be true once the identity is supplied).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute the h-expansion of h q_2 with the correct coefficient (4 alpha_1+alpha_2)/24 for the f'(a)^3 q_1^{(0,3)} term and with the extra term alpha_2 h^4 f'(a)^3 (d q_1^{(0,2)}/dx)/16 from the variation of q_1^{(0,2)}(x,x) along the diagonal, and prove the identity q_1^{(0,3)}(x,x) = (3/2)(d/dx)q_1^{(0,2)}(x,x) implied by eq:construct; these make the h^4 terms cancel and yield the o(h^4) (in fact O(h^5)) error.
issues.overall_effect: The error guarantee of thm:construct for the three-point rule is not established by the printed derivation, and the accompanying claim that the same q_2 construction turns any symmetric affinely exact q_1 into an o(h^4) rule rests on the same computation.
issues.title: h^4 expansion proving the o(h^4) error of the three-point rule is miscalculated
issues.why_classification: Correcting the algebra alone leaves a non-vanishing h^4 term and destroys the claim, so a short but nontrivial identity about the diagonal derivatives of q_1 must be added; the statement, rate and scope then survive, which rules out both a routine local fix and any major loss.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: in $\xi_k$ and hence must be linearly independent. This unique solution yields
an $n$-point quadrature formula that is exact on polynomials of order $n-1$

issues.failure_explanation: From the paper's own expansion of the k-th term, matching the Taylor coefficients of I[f] up to h^{n+1} needs the displayed equations (j = 2,...,n) together with the j = 0,1 condition sum_k alpha_k = 1; the proof claims the matching 'amounts to' the (n-1)x(n-1) system and silently drops this condition. Without it the rule is not even exact for constants, so the asserted exactness on polynomials of order n-1 does not follow, and the argument would apply verbatim to even n where the conclusion is false (for n = 4 the system solves to alpha = (-113/60, 99/28, -9/35), whose sum is 586/420 != 1); a step using the hypothesis that n is odd is missing. The uniqueness claim is also unsupported: vectors obtained by evaluating polynomials of different degrees at the same nodes need not be independent (e.g. xi^2 and xi^3 at nodes 0 and 1), so the stated reason does not show the system is non-singular.

failure_location.quote: $I[f]$ up to order $h^{n+1}$ amounts to the $(n-1)\times(n-1)$ linear equation

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Include the condition sum_k alpha_k = 1 in the matching and show the unique solution of the displayed system satisfies it when n is odd (e.g. by exhibiting the Newton-Cotes weights as the corresponding alpha), and replace the row-independence argument by a valid one; alternatively replace the j = n equation by sum_k alpha_k = 1, which makes the derivation complete for every n >= 3.
issues.overall_effect: Corollary cor:added-4 is unproven as printed: both the identification of the constructed rules with the Newton-Cotes rules and the existence/uniqueness of the weights are unsupported. The statement itself is correct for odd n once the missing normalization check and a valid non-singularity argument are supplied.
issues.title: Newton-Cotes corollary drops the normalization condition and mis-argues uniqueness
issues.why_classification: The repair requires contained but nontrivial arguments (the missing normalization check, which is exactly what restricts the statement to odd n, and a correct non-singularity proof) and no part of the corollary needs to be given up; it is therefore more than a routine local fix but needs no new global proof architecture.
